title: Transient DNS reply multiplexing across peering gateway after failover
creator: Carmen Ortiz
description:
Summary: A Tier-1 Dedicated customer reported intermittent failures where DNS responses for tenant A were observed by tenant B after a peering gateway failover. This surfaced as cross-tenant service discovery bleed and caused live requests to route to wrong backend pools for ~3m at peak.

Impact: Customer-visible routing and service discovery drift for a small subset of requests during gateway failovers. Customer-impact classification: high. Affected deployment: Dedicated (peered VPCs via Redwood peering gateways), regional (us-west-2).

Reproduce (high-level):
1) Create two tenants (T-A, T-B) with peering enabled through Redwood peering gateway.
2) Configure tenant-local DNS forwarders and short-lived NAT mappings on gateway.
3) Simulate gateway failover by killing peering-gw process and letting orchestration relocate it.
4) Observe that a small fraction of UDP TCP/53 responses are answered from conntrack/NAT entries left on old instance and delivered into the overlay after the new instance reattaches, resulting in responses being associated with other tenant sockets when ephemeral 5-tuple collisions occur.

Root cause: Race between gateway failover reattachment + ephemeral conntrack state migration and our peering reconciliation path. Specifically: (a) conntrack entries for DNAT'ed DNS replies remained on old gateway instance and were reintroduced into the overlay after the new gateway re-established tunnels, and (b) our peering gateway SRC/DST hashing allowed identical ephemeral ports between tenants on different host NICs, producing a 5-tuple collision when the old conntrack state replayed. The reconciliation code attempted to re-apply routes but did not ensure conntrack namespace isolation or strict tenant affinity during transition.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Emergency customer mitigation: performed a controlled peering gateway recycle on the customer's Dedicated cluster to purge conntrack state and drain existing ephemeral mappings (manual runbook step).
- Cluster-level temporary workaround: disabled gateway fast-reattach in the orchestration manifest for the affected region to allow conntrack TTL expiration before reattachment (reduction of failover speed).

Permanent fix implemented in branch: fix/gw-tenant-conntrack-isolation-51877
- Introduced per-tenant conntrack namespaces on gateway VMs (namespace name = tenant-id) to guarantee state isolation.
- Added idempotent sequence number to peering route reconciliation to prevent stale route replays during transitional states.
- Hardened DNAT/PNAT allocation to include tenant-id in ephemeral source port hashing to avoid cross-tenant 5-tuple collisions.
- Added end-to-end integration tests in infra/peering/ that simulate kill/reattach and assert zero cross-tenant responses.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests: conntrack namespace allocation and cleanup (100% path coverage for new code).
- Integration tests: synthetic failover harness reproduces previous bleed locally and now shows zero cross-tenant DNS replies in 5000 iterations.
- Staging rollout: beta roll started 2026-02-28 to controlled fleet (10% of gw nodes) with monitoring alarms for cross-tenant DNS indicators and conntrack leak rates.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (10%) -> 2026-02-28 (passed)
- Regional ramp (50%) -> 2026-03-03 (observed stable metrics)
- Global rollout -> target 2026-03-08 (subject to final runbook sign-off)

Rollback strategy: immediate feature toggle to restore previous behavior and automated conntrack purge job in orchestration to clear ephemeral state; can revert by toggling gw-fast-reattach flag and redeploying orchestrator.

Observability additions:
- New metric: gw.conntrack.namespace_count_by_tenant
- New alert: Ratio of dns_replies_mismatch_over_total > 0.0001 over 5m in any region
- Dashboard tiles added to Console: Peering -> Gateway -> Conntrack namespace counts and DNAT port distributions.

Customer communication:
- 2026-02-19: Customer notified of in-flight mitigation and scheduled gateway recycle (support ticket #SUP-1229).
- 2026-02-28: Customer invited to staging validation; they confirmed no recurrence in their test harness.

Postmortem actions (owner assignments included):
- Add regression tests to CI that randomly assign ephemeral ports across tenants and assert zero cross-tenant mapping (owner: Priya Rao).
- Formalize runbook for controlled conntrack purge and peering gateway recycle (owner: Marcus Lee).
- Security review to ensure tenant namespace isolation meets compliance (owner: Security Team)

Related artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/869 (fix/gw-tenant-conntrack-isolation-51877)
- Staging dashboard link (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/d/peering-gw-staging
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Peering+Gateway+Conntrack+Runbook
